public_rationale: A bipartisan coalition of 36 attorneys general formally opposed a moratorium on state AI laws during the current debate. That supports substantial opposition in both parties. Trump's continued support shows that the proposal still had powerful Republican advocates. The result therefore concerns broad bipartisan resistance, not unanimous opposition or measured voter popularity.
limitations: The precise preemption proposal is not named.
The observation window is an explicit evaluator choice.
The coalition evidence concerns public officials rather than representative voter opinion.

our_interpretation: Same thing carries forward the assertion of opposition within both Republicans and Democrats.
The ordinary reading concerns substantial bipartisan resistance to broad federal displacement of state AI protections, rather than opposition to every possible federal AI standard.

Because the sentence describes an ongoing proposal debate without dates, the observation window is November 1 through December 9, 2025: the latest completed month and the elapsed portion of the posting month.
criteria.support_condition: Contemporaneous collective actions or statements establish substantial opposition among Republican and Democratic officials to broad preemption.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Representative records establish broad acceptance within either party, with opposition too limited to sustain the stated characterization.
